findings.title: Async create can persist an unmodified request object to legacy storage
findings.body: The unified store returns `created`, which may contain server-assigned fields such as the generated name, UID, and resource version, but the asynchronous legacy write receives the original `obj`. In particular, Kubernetes create requests using `generateName` may not have a concrete name in `obj`; the legacy write can therefore fail or create a different record instead of mirroring the successful unified write. Write the object returned by unified storage, or otherwise ensure the legacy write uses the exact persisted object.

findings.title: Async update replays the request instead of the unified result
findings.body: The legacy update receives the original `objInfo` after the unified update has completed, rather than an update wrapper containing the object returned by unified storage. The two stores can independently read different old versions and apply the request, so fields or metadata selected/assigned by unified storage can diverge in legacy storage; concurrent updates make this especially likely. Mirror the persisted unified result when writing legacy, as the previous implementation did.

findings.title: Delete discards the per-request logger from its context
findings.body: This constructs the operation context with `d.Log` instead of the `log` value that includes the object name, kind, and method. The asynchronous legacy delete inherits that context, so its logs lose the operation fields and cannot be reliably correlated with the request. Use `log` here, as the other operations do.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses the object name as the kind label
findings.body: On successful storage deletion, this call passes `name` where the other paths pass `options.Kind` to `recordStorageDuration`. The metric therefore labels successful deletes by object name instead of resource kind, creating high-cardinality labels and making delete metrics inconsistent (and potentially overwhelming the metrics backend). Pass `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Delete-collection legacy duration is recorded as storage duration
findings.body: The asynchronous legacy delete-collection result is recorded with `recordStorageDuration`, even though the operation ran against `d.Legacy`. This attributes legacy latency and errors to unified-storage metrics and leaves the legacy metric unreported. Record it with `recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Storage failures are recorded as legacy failures for create and update
findings.body: When `Storage.Create` or `Storage.Update` fails, these branches call `recordLegacyDuration` even though no legacy operation was attempted. This misattributes unified-storage failures to the legacy backend and omits them from storage error metrics, undermining the metrics used to monitor migration health. Record the failure with `recordStorageDuration`.
